items.followUp: What does RADAR stand for? Write one use of RADAR.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of the term LIDAR.
rubric.description: Expands LIDAR as Light Detection and Ranging.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct expansion.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of an application of LIDAR.
rubric.description: States a valid use, such as measuring distance or surveying/mapping.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one valid use.

modelAnswer: LIDAR stands for Light Detection and Ranging.
It is used to measure the distance of objects (and can be used for surveying and mapping).

items.followUp: Write two ways of representing a vector, and state what the arrowhead shows.

rubric.why: Checks the graphical method of representing a vector.
rubric.description: States that a vector can be represented by a directed line segment (arrow).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the arrow method.

rubric.why: Checks the symbolic method of representing a vector.
rubric.description: States that a vector can be represented by a bold letter or a letter with an arrow over it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either accepted symbolic notation.

modelAnswer: A vector can be represented graphically by a directed line segment (an arrow); its length represents magnitude and its arrowhead represents direction.
A vector can also be represented by a bold letter or by a letter with an arrow over it.

items.followUp: Define one watt in terms of work and time.

rubric.why: Checks the SI unit of work.
rubric.description: Identifies the joule (J) as the SI unit of work.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of one joule.
rubric.description: Defines one joule as the work done by a force of 1 N in moving an object 1 m in the direction of the force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the complete force, displacement and direction definition.

modelAnswer: The SI unit of work is the joule (J).
One joule is the work done when a force of 1 N displaces an object by 1 m in the direction of the force.

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and write its equation.

rubric.why: Checks that gravitational potential energy is associated with position in a gravitational field.
rubric.description: Defines gravitational potential energy as energy due to an object's position (or height) in a gravitational field.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: Checks the equation for gravitational potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct equation.

modelAnswer: Gravitational potential energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its position in a gravitational field.

items.followUp: State Newton's second law in terms of momentum and write its equation.

rubric.why: Checks the verbal relation between force and momentum.
rubric.description: States that force is the rate of change of momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct statement.

rubric.why: Checks the mathematical expression of the relation.
rubric.description: Writes force as change in momentum divided by time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct equation.

rubric.why: Checks the momentum expression used to obtain the force relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying momentum as mass multiplied by velocity.

rubric.why: Checks the resulting relation for constant mass.
rubric.description: Shows that the relation gives F = ma for constant mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct resulting relation.

modelAnswer: According to Newton's second law, the force acting on an object is equal to the rate of change of its momentum.
Since momentum p = mv, for mass m changing velocity from u to v in time t:
F = change in momentum / time = (mv − mu) / t.
For constant mass, F = m(v − u) / t = ma.

items.followUp: Define the center of gravity and state its position in a uniform circular disc.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of center of gravity.
rubric.description: Defines it as the point through which the whole weight of a body may be considered to act.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the complete definition; award 1 mark if only the point or the whole-weight idea is stated.

rubric.why: Checks the position of the center of gravity for a uniform square.
rubric.description: Locates it at the intersection of the diagonals, at the square's center.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct location; award 1 mark for stating only the center or only the intersection of the diagonals.

modelAnswer: The center of gravity of a body is the point through which its whole weight may be considered to act.
For a uniform square, the center of gravity is at the intersection of its diagonals, which is the center of the square.

items.followUp: Name any four SI base quantities and give their SI units.

rubric.why: Checks recall of the SI base quantities.
rubric.description: Names any four distinct SI base quantities.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for four correct quantities; award 1 mark for two or three.

modelAnswer: Four SI base quantities are length, mass, time and electric current.

items.followUp: What is the prefix kilo? Give its symbol and value.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of a prefix in measurement.
rubric.description: Defines prefixes as words or symbols placed before units to show multiples or submultiples.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a prefix is added before a unit and indicates a multiple or submultiple.

rubric.why: Checks the practical purpose of prefixes.
rubric.description: Explains that prefixes make very large or very small measurements easier to express.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid explanation of their usefulness.

modelAnswer: Prefixes are words or symbols placed before units to indicate multiples or submultiples of the units.
They are useful for expressing very large or very small measurements conveniently.
